```{python}
# A SIBLING of sample_summary, not a step downstream of it: both read create_centroids'
# stores directly, so neither blocks the other and neither can invalidate the other's
# output. The split exists because consensus grouping is the part that gets iterated on
# — inside sample_summary, changing the linkage or the cut meant re-rendering every
# sample's fourteen per-sample slides to look at one heatmap.
#
# This deck reads CENTROIDS ONLY. No clustered zarr, no counts matrix, no per-cell
# anything: sample and cluster ride in each store's obs, so the cohort is recoverable
# without opening a zarr at all. That is what makes it cheap enough to re-render on
# every change to the grouping.
#
# THE DECK READS THE GROUPING, IT DOES NOT DEFINE IT — with one deliberate exception,
# stated here because the rule matters more than the exception. A consensus cluster id
# is an analytical artifact: it is a label you annotate against, do DE within, and cite,
# so it must not move when someone edits a caption. The authority is
# assets/consensus_clusters.csv, committed. What this deck does when that file has no
# rows is PROPOSE one — it emits consensus_scaffold.csv from the cut below, which you
# read against these slides, edit, and promote by committing. Once the asset has rows it
# wins outright and the cut is not consulted. So the exception is bounded: the deck
# defines a grouping only while no committed one exists, and it always publishes what it
# used.
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import yaml
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle
from scipy.cluster.hierarchy import dendrogram, fcluster, leaves_list, linkage
from scipy.spatial.distance import squareform

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 200, "savefig.dpi": 200})

# One slide's figure, in inches, matching the other decks.
FIGSIZE = (9.0, 4.3)

# How many consensus clusters the proposed cut takes. A knob with a default rather than
# something derived: no internal criterion (silhouette, gap) knows what a cell type is,
# and on the two test ROIs the choice between 5 and 6 is exactly the choice between
# "follicle" as one group and "oocyte" and "granulosa" as two — a biological judgment
# made by reading the marker evidence on the slides below, not a number to optimise.
#
# It only ever affects the SCAFFOLD. Once assets/consensus_clusters.csv has rows, this is
# not consulted at all.
CONSENSUS_K = 5

# Average linkage on 1 - Spearman between cluster centroids. Average rather than Ward
# because Ward's criterion is defined on Euclidean distances and is not meaningful on a
# correlation distance; average is what sample_summary already uses for its within-sample
# dendrogram, so the two decks order clusters by the same rule.
LINKAGE_METHOD = "average"

# Every sample's centroid store, staged flat into this notebook's working directory by
# the Nextflow process. Globbing is the whole input contract, as it is for the other
# decks. Keyed on obs["sample"] rather than the file name.
STORES = sorted(Path(".").glob("*_centroids.h5ad"))
if not STORES:
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "No *_centroids.h5ad staged next to the notebook. This deck reads "
        "create_centroids' stores — point --samplesheet at its handoff sheet.")

# The per-sample resolution table, staged under the fixed name. The cohort matrix is
# built at the resolution chosen for each sample, so this decides which rows of each
# store are read — it is a required input, not a param with a default.
RESOLUTIONS_CSV = Path("chosen_resolutions.csv")
if not RESOLUTIONS_CSV.exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"{RESOLUTIONS_CSV} not staged beside the notebook.")
_resolutions = pd.read_csv(RESOLUTIONS_CSV)
DEFAULT_RESOLUTION = 0.5
OVERRIDES = (dict(zip(_resolutions["sample"].astype(str),
                      _resolutions["resolution"].astype(float)))
             if len(_resolutions) else {})

# The two evidence families, the same assets and the same forms sample_summary uses, so
# a consensus cluster is named by the rule that names a per-sample cluster. Nothing here
# is a second definition: the marker cut, the reference and the assignment rule are all
# that deck's, applied to groups instead of clusters.
MARKER_MAX_SCORE = 1
_scored = yaml.safe_load(Path("ovary_follicle_markers.yaml").read_text())
MARKER_SETS = {name: sorted(g for g, s in genes.items()
                            if s is not None and s <= MARKER_MAX_SCORE)
               for name, genes in _scored.items()}
REFERENCE = pd.read_csv("ovary_reference_major.csv.gz", index_col=0)

# The immune subtype centroids (Data S7), read for one panel below. Kept separate from
# REFERENCE rather than concatenated into it: these four are a decomposition of the
# Immune column, not four more peers of it, so folding them in would let a subtype win
# the argmax for a group and displace a major type.
IMMUNE_REFERENCE = pd.read_csv("ovary_reference_immune.csv.gz", index_col=0)

# The committed grouping. Rows are the authority; a header-only sheet means none exists
# yet and the deck proposes one. Same convention as cell_type_annotations.csv.
CONSENSUS_CSV = Path("consensus_clusters.csv")
CURATED = pd.read_csv(CONSENSUS_CSV) if CONSENSUS_CSV.exists() else pd.DataFrame()

UNASSIGNED = "unassigned"


def md_table(df, index_label=None):
    """Render a DataFrame as a markdown table.

    The same hand-built table sample_summary uses, and for the same reason: df.style is
    HTML-only and renders as nothing in pptx, while df.to_markdown needs tabulate, which
    is NOT in the pipeline container — it fails as an ImportError inside a cell that
    `error: true` turns into a traceback slide while the render still exits 0.

    Wrapped in blank lines so the pipes start their own block. Without them Pandoc reads
    them as a lazy continuation of the caption paragraph above and prints them verbatim
    instead of building a table.
    """
    frame = df.reset_index() if index_label else df
    if index_label:
        frame = frame.rename(columns={frame.columns[0]: index_label})
    header = "| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in frame.columns) + " |"
    rule = "| " + " | ".join("---" for _ in frame.columns) + " |"
    rows = ["| " + " | ".join(str(v) for v in row) + " |"
            for row in frame.itertuples(index=False)]
    display(Markdown("\n".join(["", ""] + [header, rule] + rows + ["", ""])))
```

```{python}
# ── The cohort matrix ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One row per (sample, cluster) at that sample's chosen resolution. Both the summed
# CP10K and the summed cell count are carried, because a GROUP's centroid is the
# row-wise sum of its members' sums over the summed n_cells — the additive property
# create_centroids stores sums for. Averaging the members' centroids instead would
# weight a 200-cell cluster like a 20,000-cell one.
sums, cells, rows = [], [], []
genes = None
for path in STORES:
    store = ad.read_h5ad(path)
    sample = str(store.obs["sample"].iloc[0])
    resolution = OVERRIDES.get(sample, DEFAULT_RESOLUTION)
    block = store[store.obs["resolution"].astype(str) == f"{resolution:.2f}"]
    if block.n_obs == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{sample}: centroid store holds no rows at resolution {resolution:.2f} — "
            f"it carries {sorted(store.obs['resolution'].astype(str).unique())}.")
    if genes is None:
        genes = list(block.var_names)
    elif list(block.var_names) != genes:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{sample}: centroid store has a different gene set than the samples before "
            f"it. The cohort matrix is one frame over one panel; a store narrowed by "
            f"--n_top_genes cannot be compared against a whole-panel one.")
    matrix = np.asarray(block.X.todense() if hasattr(block.X, "todense") else block.X)
    for i, cluster in enumerate(block.obs["cluster_v1"].astype(str)):
        sums.append(matrix[i])
        cells.append(int(block.obs["n_cells"].iloc[i]))
        rows.append({"sample": sample, "cluster_v1": cluster,
                     "resolution": f"{resolution:.2f}", "label": f"{sample}:{cluster}"})

META = pd.DataFrame(rows)
SUMS = np.vstack(sums)
NCELLS = np.array(cells)
LABELS = list(META["label"])

# Cluster centroids, in the atlas pseudobulk form: summed CP10K over summed cells, then
# log1p. Identical to what sample_summary draws its own slides from.
CENTROIDS = pd.DataFrame(np.log1p(SUMS / NCELLS[:, None]), index=LABELS, columns=genes)

# Spearman rather than Pearson, for the reason sample_summary gives: a targeted panel's
# centroids are dominated by a few very high-expressing genes, which set a Pearson r
# almost on their own, while ranks weight the whole panel.
CORR = CENTROIDS.T.corr(method="spearman")
DISTANCE = 1 - CORR.to_numpy()
np.fill_diagonal(DISTANCE, 0.0)
Z = linkage(squareform(DISTANCE, checks=False), method=LINKAGE_METHOD)
ORDER = leaves_list(Z)

display(Markdown(
    f"# Cohort\n\n{META['sample'].nunique()} samples · {len(LABELS)} clusters · "
    f"{len(genes):,} genes · {int(NCELLS.sum()):,} cells"
))
```

## Cohort cluster centroid correlation

```{python}
display(Markdown(
    f"Spearman correlation between every pair of cluster centroids across the cohort, "
    f"over all {len(genes):,} genes. Rows and columns are ordered by average linkage on "
    f"1 − r, symmetrically. The strip along the top marks which sample each cluster "
    f"comes from."
))

fig, (strip_ax, ax) = plt.subplots(
    2, 1, figsize=FIGSIZE, height_ratios=[1, 22], gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.02})

ordered = [LABELS[i] for i in ORDER]
samples = sorted(META["sample"].unique())
palette = plt.get_cmap("tab10")(np.linspace(0, 1, 10))[:len(samples)]
sample_of = dict(zip(META["label"], META["sample"]))
strip = np.array([[samples.index(sample_of[lab]) for lab in ordered]])
strip_ax.imshow(strip, aspect="auto", cmap=plt.matplotlib.colors.ListedColormap(palette),
                vmin=0, vmax=max(len(samples) - 1, 1))
strip_ax.set_xticks([]); strip_ax.set_yticks([])
for spine in strip_ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)

image = ax.imshow(CORR.loc[ordered, ordered].to_numpy(), cmap="viridis", aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(ordered)))
ax.set_xticklabels(ordered, rotation=90, fontsize=3)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(ordered)))
ax.set_yticklabels(ordered, fontsize=3)
fig.colorbar(image, ax=[strip_ax, ax], fraction=0.025, label="Spearman r")
handles = [Rectangle((0, 0), 1, 1, color=palette[i]) for i in range(len(samples))]
strip_ax.legend(handles, samples, loc="lower left", bbox_to_anchor=(0, 1.05),
                ncol=min(len(samples), 6), fontsize=4, frameon=False)
plt.show()
plt.close(fig)
```

## The proposed grouping

```{python}
# The cut, and whether the curated sheet overrides it. Computed here rather than in a
# slide function because the composition and annotation sections below both read it.
proposed = fcluster(Z, CONSENSUS_K, criterion="maxclust")
PROPOSED = {label: f"C{group}" for label, group in zip(LABELS, proposed)}

if len(CURATED):
    missing = {"sample", "cluster_v1", "consensus_id"} - set(CURATED.columns)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"{CONSENSUS_CSV} missing column(s): {sorted(missing)}")
    curated_map = {f"{r.sample}:{r.cluster_v1}": str(r.consensus_id)
                   for r in CURATED.itertuples()}
    # A cluster the sheet does not name is unassigned rather than silently taking the
    # proposed group: a partially-curated sheet must not read as a whole grouping.
    ASSIGNMENT = {label: curated_map.get(label, UNASSIGNED) for label in LABELS}
    SOURCE = "curated"
else:
    ASSIGNMENT = dict(PROPOSED)
    SOURCE = "proposed"

META["consensus_id"] = META["label"].map(ASSIGNMENT)
CONSENSUS_IDS = sorted(set(META["consensus_id"]) - {UNASSIGNED},
                       key=lambda c: (len(c), c))

display(Markdown(
    f"Average-linkage dendrogram over the same 1 − r distances, cut at "
    f"**{CONSENSUS_K}** groups. "
    + (f"`consensus_clusters.csv` carries {len(CURATED)} rows, so **that grouping is "
       f"used** and this cut is shown only as the alternative it replaced."
       if SOURCE == "curated" else
       "`consensus_clusters.csv` has no rows, so **this cut is used** and is published "
       "as `consensus_scaffold.csv` to be edited and committed.")
))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=FIGSIZE)
dendrogram(Z, labels=LABELS, ax=ax, leaf_font_size=3.5,
           color_threshold=Z[-(CONSENSUS_K - 1), 2] if CONSENSUS_K > 1 else 0)
ax.set_ylabel("1 − Spearman r", fontsize=6)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=5)
plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=90)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.close(fig)
```

## Consensus cluster membership

```{python}
display(Markdown(
    f"Each consensus cluster's members, its cell count, and how many samples it draws "
    f"from. A group spanning one sample where others span several is the signal to "
    f"look at: with donor and slide confounded in this cohort it may be a real "
    f"sample-specific population or it may be batch, and this table cannot tell them "
    f"apart."
))

membership = []
for consensus_id in CONSENSUS_IDS:
    members = META[META["consensus_id"] == consensus_id]
    membership.append({
        "consensus_id": consensus_id,
        "clusters": len(members),
        "samples": members["sample"].nunique(),
        "cells": int(NCELLS[[LABELS.index(l) for l in members["label"]]].sum()),
        "members": ", ".join(members["label"]),
    })
MEMBERSHIP = pd.DataFrame(membership)
md_table(MEMBERSHIP)
```

```{python}
# ── Consensus centroids and their evidence ────────────────────────────────────
# The row-wise sum, which is the whole reason create_centroids stores sums: a consensus
# cluster's profile is its members' summed CP10K over their summed cells. No re-reading
# of any zarr, and identical to what clustering those cells together would have given.
group_sums, group_cells = [], []
for consensus_id in CONSENSUS_IDS:
    idx = [LABELS.index(l) for l in META["label"][META["consensus_id"] == consensus_id]]
    group_sums.append(SUMS[idx].sum(axis=0))
    group_cells.append(NCELLS[idx].sum())
GROUP_CELLS = np.array(group_cells)
GROUP_CENTROIDS = pd.DataFrame(
    np.log1p(np.vstack(group_sums) / GROUP_CELLS[:, None]),
    index=CONSENSUS_IDS, columns=genes)

# Both evidence families in one frame, exactly as sample_summary builds it: marker means
# for the follicle types the reference does not contain, reference correlations for the
# major types the markers say nothing about. The two are on different scales, which does
# not matter — the assignment reads each column separately.
reference_genes = [g for g in REFERENCE.index if g in GROUP_CENTROIDS.columns]
evidence = pd.DataFrame({
    cell_type: GROUP_CENTROIDS[reference_genes].T.corrwith(
        REFERENCE.loc[reference_genes, cell_type], method="spearman")
    for cell_type in REFERENCE.columns})
for set_name, set_genes in MARKER_SETS.items():
    present = [g for g in set_genes if g in GROUP_CENTROIDS.columns]
    evidence[set_name] = (GROUP_CENTROIDS[present].mean(axis=1) if present
                          else np.nan)
EVIDENCE = evidence
```

## Consensus clusters vs cell type evidence

```{python}
display(Markdown(
    f"Each consensus cluster against both evidence families, over {len(reference_genes):,} "
    f"genes shared with the reference. The four major types are Spearman correlations of "
    f"the group centroid; the three follicle sets are the mean of that set's markers at "
    f"quality score {MARKER_MAX_SCORE}. Each column is normalised on its own range — the "
    f"two families are not on one scale, and a correlation and a marker mean are not "
    f"comparable. A red box marks the group assigned to that cell type."
))

# Assignment is the argmax DOWN each column, then a greedy pass, which is
# sample_summary's rule applied to groups. Down the column asks "which group is most
# Endothelial"; across the row asks "which of the seven is this group most like" and
# answers Stromal nearly everywhere in stroma-dominated tissue. Where two types claim
# the same group, the stronger claim — the type's lead over its own runner-up, on that
# column's own 0-1 scale so a marker mean and a correlation compare — takes it, and the
# loser falls through to its next best.
scaled = EVIDENCE.apply(
    lambda col: (col - col.min()) / (col.max() - col.min())
    if col.max() > col.min() else col * 0)
claims = []
for cell_type in EVIDENCE.columns:
    ranked = scaled[cell_type].sort_values(ascending=False)
    lead = float(ranked.iloc[0] - ranked.iloc[1]) if len(ranked) > 1 else 1.0
    claims.append((lead, cell_type, list(ranked.index)))
# A cell type whose every candidate is already taken gets None, not a missing key. That
# is not an edge case here, it is the normal state whenever the cut produces fewer groups
# than the vocabulary has types: at k=5 against 7 types, two types cannot be represented
# at all. Recording it as None and naming those types on the slide is the honest report —
# silently dropping them would show a heatmap where two columns have no box and nothing
# says why, and indexing them would raise inside a cell that `error: true` turns into a
# traceback slide while the render still exits 0.
ASSIGNED, taken = {}, set()
for _lead, cell_type, ranked in sorted(claims, reverse=True):
    ASSIGNED[cell_type] = next((c for c in ranked if c not in taken), None)
    if ASSIGNED[cell_type] is not None:
        taken.add(ASSIGNED[cell_type])
UNREPRESENTED = [t for t, c in ASSIGNED.items() if c is None]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=FIGSIZE)
image = ax.imshow(scaled.to_numpy(), cmap="magma", aspect="auto", vmin=0, vmax=1)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(EVIDENCE.columns)))
ax.set_xticklabels(EVIDENCE.columns, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=6)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(EVIDENCE.index)))
ax.set_yticklabels([f"{c} (n={GROUP_CELLS[i]:,})" for i, c in enumerate(EVIDENCE.index)],
                   fontsize=6)
for column, cell_type in enumerate(EVIDENCE.columns):
    consensus_id = ASSIGNED.get(cell_type)
    # No box for a type the cut left unrepresented; the caption names it instead.
    if consensus_id is None:
        continue
    row = list(EVIDENCE.index).index(consensus_id)
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((column - 0.5, row - 0.5), 1, 1, fill=False,
                           edgecolor="#d62728", linewidth=1.2))
for row in range(len(EVIDENCE.index)):
    for column in range(len(EVIDENCE.columns)):
        ax.text(column, row, f"{EVIDENCE.iloc[row, column]:.2f}", ha="center",
                va="center", fontsize=4.5,
                color="white" if scaled.iloc[row, column] < 0.6 else "black")
fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, fraction=0.025, label="column-normalised")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.close(fig)

if UNREPRESENTED:
    display(Markdown(
        f"**{len(UNREPRESENTED)} of {len(EVIDENCE.columns)} cell types are "
        f"unrepresented at this cut: {', '.join(sorted(UNREPRESENTED))}.** A group "
        f"answers for at most one cell type, so a cut into {len(EVIDENCE.index)} groups "
        f"cannot name {len(EVIDENCE.columns)} types. Raise `CONSENSUS_K` if these are "
        f"expected to be present and distinct — the deck cannot separate two types that "
        f"share a group."
    ))
```

## Consensus clusters vs immune subtypes

```{python}
# The one place this deck says anything about immune subtypes, and it is deliberately
# NOT a subtyping section. Measured on the test ROIs, the immune compartment does not
# split into subtypes at any cut: it is the same two clusters from k=5 through k=9, and
# at k=10 it splits BY SAMPLE (the confound) rather than by subtype. So there is nothing
# to subtype here, and a section claiming otherwise would be inventing structure.
#
# What aggregation does buy is depth. A consensus group's centroid is built from
# thousands of cells, so this correlation is decisive where the per-cell version is not:
# on the test ROIs the immune group's margin over its runner-up is 0.068, against a
# median 0.011 per cell. That is the "aggregate before correlating" result, and it is
# why this panel is at the consensus level and not in sample_summary.
#
# Every group is shown, not just the immune one, and that IS the diagnostic: the S7
# signal should concentrate in the group the major reference called Immune. If it does
# not, the reference is not discriminating and no call built on it means anything.
immune_genes = [g for g in IMMUNE_REFERENCE.index if g in GROUP_CENTROIDS.columns]
IMMUNE_EVIDENCE = pd.DataFrame({
    subtype: GROUP_CENTROIDS[immune_genes].T.corrwith(
        np.log1p(IMMUNE_REFERENCE.loc[immune_genes, subtype]), method="spearman")
    for subtype in IMMUNE_REFERENCE.columns})

immune_group = ASSIGNED.get("Immune")
display(Markdown(
    f"Spearman correlation between each consensus cluster's centroid and the four immune "
    f"subtypes of Data S7, over {len(immune_genes):,} shared genes. "
    + (f"The group called Immune is **{immune_group}**; a red box marks its strongest "
       f"subtype. " if immune_group else "No group was assigned to Immune. ")
    + "Unlike the heatmap above, all four columns are the same statistic and share one "
      "colour scale. Read the ORDERING within a row, not the absolute values: the four "
      "profiles are all immune cells and correlate highly with almost anything, and the "
      "NK and T centroids correlate with each other at 0.924 over this panel, so those "
      "two cannot be told apart at any depth by any metric."
))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=FIGSIZE)
image = ax.imshow(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.to_numpy(), cmap="viridis", aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.columns)))
ax.set_xticklabels(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.columns, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=6)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.index)))
ax.set_yticklabels([f"{c} (n={GROUP_CELLS[i]:,})" for i, c in enumerate(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.index)],
                   fontsize=6)
for row in range(len(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.index)):
    for column in range(len(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.columns)):
        ax.text(column, row, f"{IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.iloc[row, column]:.3f}", ha="center",
                va="center", fontsize=5, color="white")
if immune_group is not None:
    row = list(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.index).index(immune_group)
    column = list(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.columns).index(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.loc[immune_group].idxmax())
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((column - 0.5, row - 0.5), 1, 1, fill=False,
                           edgecolor="#d62728", linewidth=1.4))
fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, fraction=0.025, label="Spearman r")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.close(fig)

if immune_group is not None:
    ranked = IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.loc[immune_group].sort_values(ascending=False)
    display(Markdown(
        f"**{immune_group}** ({GROUP_CELLS[list(IMMUNE_EVIDENCE.index).index(immune_group)]:,} "
        f"cells) is most like **{ranked.index[0]}** at r={ranked.iloc[0]:.3f}, leading "
        f"{ranked.index[1]} by {ranked.iloc[0] - ranked.iloc[1]:.3f}. Ranking: "
        + ", ".join(f"{t} {v:.3f}" for t, v in ranked.items()) + "."
    ))
```

## Consensus composition by sample

```{python}
display(Markdown(
    "Cells per consensus cluster in each sample, as a share of that sample. Read down a "
    "column to compare one group across samples. A group thin in one sample may reflect "
    "a harsher per-sample filtering cut rather than biology — cluster_sdata resolves "
    "min_counts per sample."
))

names = {consensus_id: cell_type for cell_type, consensus_id in ASSIGNED.items()
         if consensus_id is not None}
composition = pd.DataFrame(
    0, index=sorted(META["sample"].unique()),
    columns=[f"{c} · {names.get(c, UNASSIGNED)}" for c in CONSENSUS_IDS], dtype=int)
for consensus_id in CONSENSUS_IDS:
    column = f"{consensus_id} · {names.get(consensus_id, UNASSIGNED)}"
    for sample in composition.index:
        selected = META[(META["consensus_id"] == consensus_id)
                        & (META["sample"] == sample)]
        composition.loc[sample, column] = int(
            NCELLS[[LABELS.index(l) for l in selected["label"]]].sum())

shares = composition.div(composition.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 100
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=FIGSIZE)
bottom = np.zeros(len(shares))
colours = plt.get_cmap("tab20")(np.linspace(0, 1, 20))
for i, column in enumerate(shares.columns):
    ax.bar(shares.index, shares[column], bottom=bottom, label=column,
           color=colours[i % 20])
    bottom += shares[column].to_numpy()
ax.set_ylabel("% of sample", fontsize=7)
ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
ax.legend(fontsize=5, bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1), loc="upper left", frameon=False)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.close(fig)

display(Markdown("### Cells per consensus cluster"))
md_table(composition, index_label="sample")
```

```{python}
# ── The two sheets ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Always written, whether or not a curated grouping exists, so the declared outputs are
# there either way and a run can be inspected without opening the pptx.
scaffold = pd.DataFrame({
    "sample": META["sample"],
    "cluster_v1": META["cluster_v1"],
    "resolution": META["resolution"],
    "n_cells": [NCELLS[LABELS.index(l)] for l in META["label"]],
    # The PROPOSED cut, not the assignment in use: this sheet exists to be promoted into
    # assets/consensus_clusters.csv, and writing back the curated grouping would make it
    # a copy of its own input rather than a proposal.
    "consensus_id": META["label"].map(PROPOSED),
})
scaffold.to_csv("consensus_scaffold.csv", index=False)

annotations = EVIDENCE.copy()
annotations.insert(0, "n_cells", GROUP_CELLS)
annotations.insert(0, "cell_type", [names.get(c, "") for c in EVIDENCE.index])
annotations.insert(0, "consensus_id", EVIDENCE.index)
annotations.to_csv("consensus_annotations.csv", index=False)

display(Markdown(
    f"# Outputs\n\n"
    f"`consensus_scaffold.csv` — {len(scaffold)} rows, one per (sample, cluster), "
    f"carrying the proposed grouping at k={CONSENSUS_K}. Edit it against these slides "
    f"and commit it as `assets/consensus_clusters.csv` to make a grouping authoritative.\n\n"
    f"`consensus_annotations.csv` — {len(annotations)} rows, one per consensus cluster, "
    f"with its cell type call and the evidence behind it.\n\n"
    f"Grouping in use: **{SOURCE}**."
))
```
